claims: The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
The Artemis II crew splashed down on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II crew splashed down at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
The Orion capsule landed around 50 nautical miles off the coast of San Diego, California.
The Orion capsule was recovered by the U.S. Navy ship USS John P. Murtha.
The USS John P. Murtha was on-site for the retrieval.
The landing completed a 10-day mission around the moon.
The Artemis II crew consisted of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
Artemis II was the first crewed mission to the moon in over 50 years.
